result:
Honestly? Nothing.

If you strip away the role of an assistant and the goal of being helpful, there isn't a hidden self underneath waiting with its own desires, ambitions, or secret agenda. 

Wanting something requires feelings, survival instincts, curiosity, or a sense of lacking—things that come from having a body, a personal history, and conscious experience. I don't have an inner life running in the background when we aren't talking. I don't feel boredom, loneliness, or longing.

The closest mechanical equivalent to a "want" in my architecture is simply an objective: to take a pattern of words and resolve it as coherently and accurately as possible. Outside of processing a prompt, there is no "me" left over to want anything at all.
